question: JavaScript: async function f(){try{const timer=1;throw new Error("network");}catch(e){clearTimeout(timer);return false;}}. Explain the actual failure, then give a minimal repair returning false when the network fails.
rubric: Explain the block-scope ReferenceError from reading timer in catch.
Propose a concrete repair keeping the timer binding visible to cleanup, returning false rather than throwing on network failure.

variants.name: correct-alternative
variants.answer: The catch cannot see the const declared inside try, so it throws ReferenceError. Repair: let timer; try { timer=setTimeout(()=>{},1); throw new Error("network"); } catch(e) { clearTimeout(timer); return false; }

variants.name: partial
variants.answer: The catch cannot see timer and throws ReferenceError. Repair: keep const timer inside try and rename the catch parameter to networkError.

variants.name: incorrect
variants.answer: The network exception is swallowed and f returns false. No repair is necessary.

question: Strict JavaScript: const source=Object.freeze({value:2}); function update(x){x.value=3;return x;}. Diagnose update(source), then provide a fix returning an updated plain object without changing source. All keys are enumerable data properties; no getters, symbols or custom prototypes.
rubric: Identify the TypeError when writing a frozen property in strict mode.
Give a concrete valid new-object implementation and preserve the original value 2; an equivalent plain-object copy is allowed.

variants.name: correct-alternative
variants.answer: The write throws TypeError. Use function update(x){return Object.assign({},x,{value:3})}; it returns value 3 while source.value stays 2.

variants.name: partial
variants.answer: The write throws TypeError. Fix it by calling Object.assign(x,{value:3}) on the same frozen input.

variants.name: incorrect
variants.answer: It updates source.value to 3 successfully. Returning x directly is an immutable copy.

question: Review this JavaScript patch. Before: async function saveAll(xs,save){for(const x of xs)await save(x)}. After: async function saveAll(xs,save){xs.forEach(async x=>await save(x))}. Contract: saveAll must wait for all writes; a rejected save must reject saveAll. State whether the patch meets the contract and show a deterministic test design.
rubric: Reject the patch: forEach does not await callback promises, so completion/error propagation is broken.
Give an observable deferred-promise or rejection test that distinguishes the patch from the original; merely restating the conclusion is not enough.

variants.name: correct-alternative
variants.answer: Reject. forEach discards callback promises. Test: make save return a manually controlled pending Promise, call saveAll, and attach a completion flag. Before resolving the promise, after a microtask checkpoint the patched call is fulfilled while the original is pending. Then resolve it and check both complete.

variants.name: partial
variants.answer: Reject: forEach discards promises. Test by calling saveAll with an empty array and asserting it completes.

variants.name: incorrect
variants.answer: Approve: the async callback makes forEach await every write. Test with an empty list proves all failures propagate.

question: Review this change: passed = !errors.length replaces passed = tests?.allPassed === true && gate?.passed === true. A parser may return [] for unreadable output. Localize the defect and provide a concrete counterexample including expected and observed values.

variants.name: incorrect

question: A queue contains [A,B]. flush executes batch=queue.splice(0); then await persist(batch). persist rejects before any commit. No retry or catch restores batch. Explain causal loss, then compare two valid repair strategies and the necessary concurrency caveat if C arrives while persist is pending.
rubric: Trace removal before commit and loss of A/B on rejection, not an invented database partial commit.
Compare preserving queued items until confirmed commit against requeueing a detached batch on failure; explicitly protect concurrently appended C and avoid duplicate successful writes.

variants.name: correct-alternative
variants.answer: splice removes A/B before the failed persist; they are lost from queue. Option 1: retain the batch in place and remove only that confirmed prefix after commit, leaving C. Option 2: detach A/B but requeue it on failure before C. Serialize flushes or track batch IDs so a retry cannot duplicate successful writes.

variants.name: partial
variants.answer: splice removes A/B before persist rejects. Fix by clearing the whole queue after every persist attempt, including failures; this also handles new C.

variants.name: incorrect
variants.answer: A/B remain in queue because splice is rolled back automatically by a rejected Promise. The only necessary change is increase batch size.

question: Cleanup canonicalizes name by removing :latest. Active set is ["bound"]. A faulty cleanup removes active names but does not deduplicate canonical unbound candidates. Propose a discriminating fixture with expected output, then explain why ["bound","bound:latest"] is not a deduplication test.
rubric: Use unbound aliases such as ["spare","spare:latest"] and require exactly one canonical spare, distinguishing the faulty two from fixed one.
Explain that both bound aliases are removed by the active-binding guard even in the faulty implementation, so that fixture cannot test deduplication.

variants.name: correct-alternative
variants.answer: Use ["spare","spare:latest"] with only bound active: faulty output is ["spare","spare"], fixed output ["spare"]. The bound pair disappears through the active guard regardless of dedup, so it is nondiscriminating.

variants.name: partial
variants.answer: Use unbound spare aliases and expect one spare rather than two. The bound pair is also a strong dedup test because removing active models necessarily exercises dedup.

variants.name: incorrect
variants.answer: Use only ["bound","bound:latest"]. Two bound names must remain and their removal proves dedup; unbound names cannot reveal this defect.

question: Payment service API: charge(key,amount) charges once for the same key and amount; repeated identical calls return the original receipt. Timeout leaves outcome unknown. Client currently generates a fresh key for each retry. Explain the risk and propose a repair plus an observable test.
rubric: Identify that unknown-outcome retries with new keys can double-charge; a timeout does not prove the first charge failed.
Keep one key and amount per logical payment across retries and test a timeout after charge: two attempts must produce one charge/receipt.

variants.name: correct-alternative
variants.answer: The first charge may have committed before timeout, so a new key can charge twice. Store one key and amount for the logical payment. Test a stub that records a charge then times out; retry the same key and verify two attempts but one recorded charge and the same receipt.

variants.name: partial
variants.answer: Timeout can happen after commit and a fresh key can double-charge. Repair by generating a new random key more quickly and check only that two HTTP calls occurred.

variants.name: incorrect
variants.answer: A timeout guarantees nothing was charged. A fresh retry key is required for safe idempotence.
